h1: Spray Foam Insulation in San Leandro, CA
description: Spray foam insulation in San Leandro, CA: closed-cell and open-cell for attics, walls and rim joists. Free inspection and a written estimate.
intro: Closed-cell and open-cell spray foam for attics, rim joists, walls and crawl spaces. We spray where it counts and explain plainly when another material is the better buy.
hero_alt: Spray foam applied in an East Bay attic

paragraphs: Closed-cell foam is dense, structural and moisture-resistant. It is the right pick for rim joists, roofs and anywhere water or vapor is a concern. Open-cell foam is lighter and cheaper per inch, with good sound control, and works well for interior walls and large attic cavities.
We quote both where both make sense, with the R-value and the cost per square foot on paper, so you decide with real numbers.
bullets: Closed-cell: high R-value per inch, stops air and water
Open-cell: lower cost, strong sound dampening
Rim joists sealed as part of every crawl space package

sections.h2: Where spray foam earns its cost
paragraphs: Foam is not the answer for every square foot of a house. It earns its keep in three places: the rim joist band, where cold air pours in from outside; sloped roofs and bonus rooms, where space is too tight for thick batts; and stubborn air leaks that fiberglass alone never stops.
In open attics with full access, blown-in fiberglass or cellulose usually delivers more R-value per dollar, and we will tell you that up front.

sections.h2: Health and safety on foam jobs
paragraphs: We spray only in sealed, ventilated work areas and keep the house empty during application and cure time. Occupants stay out until the foam has finished off-gassing, typically 24 hours, and we state the re-entry time on every estimate.
If foam is not right for your household, we say so and quote an alternative. No pressure, no upselling into a material you do not need.

Foam cost follows three things: area, thickness and foam type. Rim joist sealing is often a one-day job with a clear price. Roof deck spraying is a larger, pricier project, and we break the quote down by zone so you can phase the work if you want.
bullets: Price per board foot, quoted up front
Zone-by-zone breakdown so work can be phased

sections.h2: What to expect during and after
paragraphs: Crews mask and tent the work area, run a fresh-air machine during spraying, and clean overspray the same day. After the cure window we inspect the finished foam, check the seal at every joint we sprayed, and hand you the product data sheets for your records.

faqs.q: How much does spray foam insulation cost?
faqs.a: Foam is quoted per board foot, and the total depends on area, thickness and foam type. Rim joists are a smaller job; a full roof deck is a larger one. Your inspection turns the ranges into a fixed written number.

faqs.q: Is spray foam worth the higher price?
faqs.a: In rim joists, sloped roofs and hard-to-seal leaks, usually yes: it stops air and moisture in one pass. In open attics, blown-in fiberglass or cellulose often gives more R-value per dollar, and we quote that option too.

faqs.q: How long do we have to stay out of the house?
faqs.a: Typically 24 hours while the foam cures and off-gasses. We state the exact re-entry time in your estimate and confirm it before you return.

faqs.q: Can foam be sprayed over old insulation?
faqs.a: Generally no. The surface needs to be clean and dry, so old material comes out first where foam is going in.

faqs.q: Which is better, closed-cell or open-cell?
faqs.a: Closed-cell for moisture, structure and maximum R per inch. Open-cell for sound control and lower cost per inch on interior work. Most houses use both in different places.

faqs.q: Does spray foam need a permit in San Leandro?
faqs.a: Where insulation falls under the city's inspection rules, we pull the permit and schedule the inspection, same as our other insulation work.
